description: The plot illustrates how loss changes as compute increases, comparing two methods labeled “Vanilla” and “SepLLM.” The x-axis is labeled “TFLOPs,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0.00 to 1.25 with a “1e9” multiplier shown (ticks appear at regular 0.25 intervals: 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25). The y-axis is labeled “Loss,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 2.40 to 2.75 with ticks at 0.05 increments (2.40, 2.45, 2.50, …, 2.75). The “Vanilla” series is a purple solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near the top of the axis around 2.75 at very low TFLOPs, then decreases steadily across the x-range, reaching about 2.50 at the right end near 1.25×10^9 TFLOPs. The “SepLLM” series is a red solid line with circular markers; it begins around 2.74–2.75 at very low TFLOPs, drops quickly to roughly 2.60 by around 0.2×10^9 TFLOPs, then continues a gradual decline, passing near 2.50 around roughly 0.9×10^9 TFLOPs and ending around 2.47–2.48 near 1.2–1.25×10^9 TFLOPs. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at Loss = 2.50, and green dashed vertical guides and a double-headed arrow annotate a span labeled “1.28×” near the right side of the plot.
